==English== ===Etymology 1=== {{wp}} {{wp|+am (surah)}} [[File:Sassoferrato - Jungfrun i bön.jpg|thumb|A depiction of Mary, Mother of God, praying in quiet devotion (''{{w|The Virgin in Prayer}}'' by [[w:Giovanni Battista Salvi da Sassoferrato|Sassoferrato]], {{circa2|1650|short=1}})]] {{etymon|en|id=Marie|:inh|enm:Marie|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|Marie}}, from {{der|en|fro|Marie}}, from {{der|en|la|Maria}}, from {{der|en|grc|Μαρία}}, {{m|grc|Μαριάμ}}, from post-Biblical {{der|en|he|-}} and {{der|en|arc|מַרְיָם|tr=Maryām}}, from {{der|en|hbo|מִרְיָם|tr=Miryām}}, of uncertain meaning. (See the Hebrew entry for more.) {{doublet|en|Miriam|Marie|Maria|Mariah}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|Marie||Early New English}} ====Pronunciation==== * {{enPR|mârʹē|a=RP,GA,CA}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈmɛəɹi/}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-Mary.ogg|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Wodencafe-mary.wav|a=US}} * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈmɛːɹɪj/|a=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈmɜːɹɪ/|a=Lancashire,square-nurse}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈmeɾe/|[ˈmeːɾe]|/-ɾɪ/|/-ɾi/|a=Scotland}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈmɛːɾi/|a=Wales}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈmeːɹi/|a=AU}} * {{enPR|mâʹrē|a=NZ}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈmeəɹi/|a=non-near-square}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈmiəɹi/|a=near-square}} * {{homophones|en|marry|;|Merry|merry}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛəɹi|s=2}} ====Proper noun==== {{en-proper noun|s|ies}} # {{given name|en|female|from=Aramaic,Hebrew}}. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1821|author=Lord Byron|title=Don Juan|section=Canto the Fifth: IV |passage=I have a passion for the name of '''Mary''',
For once it was a magic sound to me:
And still it half calls up the realm of fairy
Where I beheld what never was to be.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1830|author=Mary Russell Mitford|title=Our Village: Cottage Names |passage='''Mary''', which is as common as a white violet, and like that has something indestructibly sweet and simple, and fit for all wear, high or low, suits the cottage or the palace, the garden or the field, the pretty and the ugly, the old and the young;}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1996|author=w:Maeve Binchy|title=This Year It Will Be Different: A Christmas Treasury|publisher=Hachette UK|year_published=2008|isbn=9781409105404 |passage=They had called their children Ann, '''Mary''', and John as a reaction against their own fancy tricksy names. Both mothers thought these names sadly unimaginative and each blamed the child of the other for the lack of vision and style.}} #* {{RQ:NYT|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205210834/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/04/27/books/review/show-me-a-sign-ann-clare-lezotte.html|author=Meg Medina|authorlink=Meg Medina|title=A Deaf Girl Finds Her Voice on Martha's Vineyard in the 19th Century|date=2020-04-27|passage=Life on Martha’s Vineyard has been mostly ideal for 11-year-old '''Mary''' Elizabeth Lambert, the protagonist of Ann Clare LeZotte’s historical novel SHOW ME A SIGN (Scholastic, 288 pp., $18.99; ages 8 to 12).}} # {{senseid|en|Q345}} {{lb|en|religion}} The [[mother]] of [[Jesus#English:_Q302|Jesus]]; [[believe]]d in [[Christianity]] and [[Islam]] to have been a [[virgin]], and believed by most Christians to have been born herself without [[sin]], to have been [[assume]]d into [[Heaven]] without [[death]], and to [[act]] as a [[sympathetic]] [[intercessor]] for [[believer]]s. #* {{RQ:King James Version|Matthew|1|18|page=1220|column=2|text=Now the birth of [[Jesus Christ|Jeſus Chriſt]] was on this [[wise|wiſe]]: When as his mother '''Mary''' was [[espoused|eſpouſed]] to [[Joseph|Joſeph]] (before they came together) [[she|ſhee]] was found with [[child]]e of the [[Holy Ghost|holy Ghoſt]].}} # {{lb|en|biblical}} Any of several other women in the [[New Testament]], notably: ## [[Mary Magdalene]], a [[disciple]] of [[Jesus]]. ## {{w|Mary of Bethany}}, the sister of [[Lazarus]] and [[Martha]]. ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Luke|10|41|42|page=1297|column=1|text=And Jeſus anſwered, and ſaide vnto her, Martha, Martha, thou art carefull, and troubled about many things: But one thing is needefull, and '''Mary''' hath choſen that good part, which ſhall not bee taken away from her.}} # {{lb|en|Islam}} {{synonym of|en|Maryam|id=Q220716|t=The 19th [[sura]] (chapter) of the [[Qur'an]]}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|US|gay slang}} {{n-g|A term of address for a [[male]] [[homosexual]].}} {{defdate|1925}} #: {{synonyms|en|nancy|nan|Thesaurus:male homosexual}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1941|author=G.
